source.title: Modeling the Machine Learning Multiverse
source.authors: Samuel J Bell; Onno P. Kampman; Jesse Dodge; Neil D. Lawrence

record.tranche_reason: The study's own optimizer and batch-size multiverse results qualify or challenge broad claims about optimizer differences and a general large-batch gap.
record.gate_note: Tests V4 by varying learning rate and Adam epsilon for VGG-16 on CIFAR-10. Tests V5 by varying batch size and learning rate across image classifiers and datasets. Results cited from prior studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own Adam–momentum SGD comparisons and batch-size/learning-rate sweeps, qualifying V4 and testing the recipe-adaptation component of V5. It does not establish V5's fixed-epoch premise because the training budget for the batch-size study is unspecified in the supplied text.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that learning rate largely determines the Adam–SGD ranking, find little effect of Adam epsilon, and report that coordinated learning-rate/batch-size scaling maintains CIFAR accuracy. They dispute a general large-batch gap after accounting for learning rate and find no uncorrectable threshold through batch size 8192. Their Tiny ImageNet runs severely overfit. These conclusions do not establish a fixed-epoch comparison.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a multiverse sweep over optimizer hyperparameters and batch size/learning rate, not the original studies' individual training comparisons. It does not use random-label memorization or the other claim-version interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer comparison changes with learning rate; Adam epsilon has little measured effect. For batch size, test accuracy depends jointly on batch size and learning rate; dataset has the largest reported main effect, likely due to Tiny ImageNet.

fits_no_version.finding: Of 42 Tiny ImageNet runs, 22 reached training accuracy ≥0.99, and none of those exceeded 0.01 test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These Tiny ImageNet training configurations severely overfit; the aggregate result does not identify a batch-size penalty.

record.problems: Only one model is used for the optimizer comparison, and the authors describe it as a limited case study. Case study 2 discards 115 of 224 trials for training accuracy below 0.99; 9 more failed to converge. No Tiny ImageNet model trained successfully with high test accuracy. The paper states it trained only a single model for each point.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying outcomes left out. The test-accuracy contours in Fig. 4 and Fig. S4 are recorded as figure-only where the text does not state numerical values.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy using the same architectures and recipes.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity.

Language benchmarks, other adaptive optimizers and architectures, decay-schedule tuning, switching optimizers, and decoupled weight decay. The study does not establish a comparison after independently optimizing each optimizer's learning rate.
The fixed-epoch-budget premise is not established. Language models, longer-training interventions, warmup, normalization and regularization changes are not tested.
Effects of adding or removing dropout.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for these versions. Its broader dispute with an unconditional large-batch gap does not challenge V5 as written, which already allows recipe adaptation to remove the penalty. Case study 2 excludes 115 low-training-accuracy trials and nine convergence failures from 224 trials; each configuration has a single run. Numerical contour values cannot be recovered reliably from the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Other architectures, datasets, and broader optimizer tuning beyond learning rate and epsilon.
Language models, fixed epoch-budget comparisons, and the effects of longer training or normalization and regularization changes.
Sharpness measures and their relation to generalization gaps.

rows.subject: VGG-16 with batch normalization and dropout
rows.operation_detail: Compared Adam with SGD with momentum across learning rate and Adam epsilon; reports difference in test accuracy (SGD - Adam).
rows.measure: Difference in test accuracy (SGD - Adam) across the hyperparameter search
rows.value: A large region (10^-3 ≤ α ≤ 10^2) in which SGD outperforms Adam; opposite regions approximately α < 10^-3 or α > 10^2.
rows.uncertainty: Higher uncertainty in the high learning rate region; sensitivity estimates: learning rate main effect 0.990 ± 0.014 and total effect 0.996 ± 0.014; epsilon main effect -0.004 ± 0.0002 and total effect 0.008 ± 0.031.
rows.note: The text says SGD often, but not always, outperforms Adam; learning rate drives nearly all output variance and the conclusion is sensitive to learning rate. Figure 2 reports final train and test accuracies with whiskers extending to min and max, but numerical values are not stated in text.
rows.check: Split the opposing learning-rate conditions: SGD wins approximately from 10^-3 to 10^(1/2); Adam wins below or above that region, with greater uncertainty at high rates. The extracted upper boundary 10^2 is a misreading of 10^(1/2), approximately 0.316. The search itself ends at 10^0. These comparisons use a shared learning rate and do not establish the winner after separately optimizing each optimizer.

source_check.correct: Section 4.2 states SGD outperforms Adam for approximately 10^-3 ≤ α ≤ 10^(1/2), with Adam outperforming below or above this region and greater uncertainty at high learning rates. The extracted upper boundary 10^2 is incorrect.
source_check.problem: The fractional exponent 1/2 was flattened to 2; the source also gives a search range inconsistent with its stated upper crossover.

rows.subject: AlexNet
rows.operation_detail: Varied batch size and learning rate; measured test accuracy.
rows.measure: Test accuracy across learning rate and batch size
rows.note: The authors describe a consistent plateau across all models on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, with test accuracy maintained as batch size scales with learning rate; precise values are figure-only.
rows.check: Learning-rate upper bound is 10^(-1/2), approximately 0.316, rather than 10^-2. Replace 'figure only' with the text-supported mixed result: accuracy is maintained with coordinated batch-size/learning-rate scaling and decreases outside the plateau. Contours are GP predictions conditional on retaining runs with training accuracy ≥0.99; the epoch budget is unspecified.

relationships.condition: VGG-16 on CIFAR-10, shared learning rates approximately 10^-3 through 10^(1/2)
relationships.reason: R1 reports higher test accuracy for momentum SGD than Adam throughout a substantial learning-rate region, supporting the stated tendency in this setting.
relationships.display_finding: Momentum SGD led within the reported region and Adam outside it, but inconsistent learning-rate boundaries prevent a precise range.

relationships.condition: VGG-16 on CIFAR-10, shared learning rates below approximately 10^-3 or above 10^(1/2)

relationships.display_finding: Adam outperformed SGD at low learning rates, while the reported high-rate advantage had greater uncertainty and an inconsistent search-range description.
